label: PF Backlog 577
title: Eventing SSOT: contracts (envelope+seq, subscription, alert-rule, webhook signature) + Go parity
body:
## Problem / why
The bus, subscriber registry, alert rules and webhook payloads need versioned contracts before code;
Go and Python must agree byte-for-byte (A1 wire pattern).

## Goal / value
Additive contract extensions in core/contracts.py (edit) + Go mirror with parity tests.

## In scope
- Event envelope v2: add monotonic `seq` (keep occurred_at/ts + legacy fields).
- subscription schema; alert-rule schema; webhook payload + HMAC signature header.
- Go mirror (go/) + parity test (test-framework/tests/pipeline).

## Out of scope
- Breaking existing envelope fields; new Python modules under shipped roots.

## Acceptance criteria
- Go and Python required-field/shape parity tests pass; existing test_api_events stays green.

## Verification / test plan
- Parity test (mirrors test_contracts.py pattern); contract test pins events.py public symbols.

## Dependencies & links
- E1; A1 contracts (BI-PF-0393/0394).

decisions.decision: Extend the A1 contract surface additively; Go mirror + parity test; no new Python module

decisions.note: HIL approved the six BI-PF-1267 contract resolutions: unknown fields, seq, HMAC ownership, secret handling, dedupe ownership, parity tests.
HIL approved Gate 1 for BI-PF-1267 after design/spec/conformance and no blocker/major pending.
HIL approved Gate 2 after AC verification and review dispositions.
HIL acknowledged design correction from new go/pfcore/contracts.go to reuse of existing pfcore/contract mirrors; permits the second full design review.

edit only; no new Go file

_note: HIL MATERIAL_CHANGE recorded for corrected design scope.

api_impact.reason: Shared contract shapes only; no runtime API route change.

requirements: Go and Python required-field/shape parity tests pass; existing test_api_events stays green.
invariants: Wire contracts are versioned and additive.
Unknown top-level envelope fields are rejected; vendor data belongs only in extensions{}.
seq is assigned by the Go/PostgreSQL event core, never by producers; per-tenant monotonic, gaps allowed, never reused.
Cursor ordering uses seq only; occurred_at is not an ordering key.
Python and Go must agree on required fields and shapes.
Webhook signatures use constant-time HMAC over the raw body; idempotency key is event_id.

api: No public runtime API change; contract shapes are shared by event producers/consumers.
config: WEBHOOK_HMAC_KEY_REF is a secret reference (never the key); required and fail-closed at startup when webhook delivery is enabled.

security: HMAC verification uses constant-time comparison; tenant/auth fields are required in subscription/replay contracts.
observability: Contract metrics are defined but emitted by BI-PF-1270/1274, not this contract item: contract_validation_failures_total{code}, contract_parity_test_failures. Owner: platform + CI.
performance: Envelope validation is bounded and allocation-light; no large payload copies (payload_ref contract).
rollout: Additive contract fields only; ship Python and Go mirrors together.
design_pack.rollback: Revert the contract PR. Mixed-version window: producers must keep legacy fields; consumers ignore unknown extensions and reject unknown top-level fields. Do not enable webhook delivery until BI-PF-1270 ships the verifier caller.
decisions: Envelope v2 adds seq and payload reference fields additively.
Subscription/alert/webhook contracts are versioned and shared.
Go mirrors Python contracts; parity is CI-blocking.
Unknown top-level envelope fields are rejected; vendor data must use extensions{}; no silent coercion.
seq is assigned by the Go/PostgreSQL event core, never by producers; per-tenant monotonic increasing, gaps allowed, never reused; cursor uses seq > cursor, not occurred_at.
BI-PF-1267 owns webhook payload/header contract and constant-time verifier test; BI-PF-1270 owns runtime delivery and calls that verifier.
WEBHOOK_HMAC_KEY_REF is a secret reference, never the key; webhook-enabled startup fails closed when missing.
BI-PF-1267 guarantees event_id and idempotency header shape; runtime dedupe belongs to BI-PF-1270.
Python/Go parity tests must cover missing/invalid seq, cursor ordering, unknown version, and signature verification.
Go contract surface: go/pfcore/contracts.go is canonical for parity; go/contract/contract.go and pfcore.contractShapes are legacy, not extended.
Reuse existing contract owners: Python core/contracts.py and Go go/pfcore/pfcore.go contractShapes are canonical; no new go/pfcore/contracts.go.
BI-PF-1267 adds strict unknown-field parity, seq/subscription/alert/webhook parity tests, and constant-time webhook HMAC verification.
Both existing Go mirrors (go/pfcore and go/contract) must stay in lockstep with Python; parity test covers required fields across both.
guardrails: No new Python module under shipped roots.
HIL-approved open-question resolutions are binding; no unconfirmed assumption may be implemented.
Unknown top-level fields fail validation; extensions{} is the only vendor extension surface.
CL-008 authz/tenant: subscription/replay contracts require tenant + auth_ref.
Unknown-field and seq invariants have named parity tests.
No metric/alert is introduced without owner and threshold.
CL-008 reversibility: revert the contract PR; no data migration.
CL-008 SPOF/startup: no runtime component in this item; webhook startup validation is owned by BI-PF-1270.
CL-008 blast radius/dry-run: contract-only; no runtime rollout; parity tests are the dry-run proof.
CL-008 tenant isolation: tenant/auth fields are required contracts and tested.
CL-008 reuse/observability: reuse core/contracts.py and existing Go mirror; metric emission is owned by BI-PF-1270/1274.
learnings: Contract drift is caught by required-field parity tests, not by prose.

outcome: Versioned event/subscription/alert/webhook contracts with Go-Python parity.
non_goals: No runtime store/dispatcher implementation in this item.
assumptions: BI-PF-1266 design and ADR-0011 are approved.

applicability.reason: No public runtime API shape change in this contract item.
WEBHOOK_HMAC_KEY_REF is a required secret reference; runtime startup validation is owned by BI-PF-1270.
No runtime SLO in this contract-only item.
HMAC and tenant fields are security-relevant.
No data migration in contract-only item.
Revert the code change; no data migration.
No runtime component in this item.
Contract parity is covered by CI tests.

MAJOR: FR-2 acceptance ("webhook accepted and deduped by event_id") requires runtime dispatch/dedup, explicitly a non-goal and absent from affected_files; declared tests cannot satisfy it.

config_contract declares WEBHOOK_HMAC_KEY_REF (fail-closed, startup validation required) while spec_pack marks config_contract N/A "no config file change" — contradictory secret-handling contract for a security-relevant control.
Invariant "unknown fields rejected or preserved by explicit version policy" is left undecided; without a pinned policy Python/Go parity tests can pass while runtime behaviors diverge.
Monotonic `seq` invariant (assignment source, gap/ordering semantics vs occurred_at, cross-producer ordering) is not stated or tested despite checklist item 5.
Design pack does not answer guardrail checklist items 1-6, 9-10 (CL-008): no authz/tenant-boundary statement, no invariant tests, no metrics/owners for CONTRACT_INVALID/WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID.
`risks: Not specified` for a security-bearing contract change; no identified parity-drift, replay, or versioning risks with mitigations.
CL-013 constant-time HMAC comparison is asserted in design_pack.security but no test or file pins it among affected_files.
MINOR: Observability says "failures counted by code" without metric names, labels, or alert owner (CL-014 lead-time not addressed).
Rollback is "Revert the change" only; no statement on mixed-version consumers during rollout window despite additive-only claim.
FR-2 verification points to test_contracts.py for signature tests, but signature verification is runtime logic not present in declared files.
NIT: Traceability evidence for FR-1 lists core/contracts.py for both design and evidence lines; could cite the parity test explicitly.
test_api_events greenness is an AC but no explicit CI job/test list is named to run it.
SUMMARY: Design is structurally sound (additive, Go mirror, CI-blocking parity) and does not violate the language rule, but it is not ready for Gate 1.5: FR-2 acceptance exceeds declared scope, the HMAC secret contract is self-contradictory, and the unknown-field and `seq` invariants are unpinned — the top risks are contract drift that parity tests may not catch and unverifiable security acceptance criteria.

BLOCKER: review.impact_review records language-rule verdict "violates" ("New Python module in shipped root") while affected_files declare only an edit to core/contracts.py; unresolved contradiction — either an undeclared shipped-Python addition (language-rule violation) or an erroneous verdict — must be reconciled before Gate approval.
MAJOR: Residual of prior config-contract finding with new evidence: delta design_pack.contracts.config states "No new env flag in this item" while functional_spec.config_contract declares WEBHOOK_HMAC_KEY_REF (required, fail-closed, env/secret precedence, startup validation); the delta spec_pack also silently dropped the config_contract applicability row entirely — a security-relevant control with no owning spec row and an explicit "no config" denial.

test_matrix pins Go/Python parity only for the envelope (row 1); no named parity test covers subscription, alert-rule, or webhook payload/header shapes although in_scope puts them in the Go mirror, and webhook tests cite core/contracts.py only — AC "Go and Python required-field/shape parity tests pass" is not fully demonstrable for in-scope contracts.

Rollback remains "Revert the contract PR" with no mixed-version consumer guidance beyond "ship Python and Go mirrors together"; prior MAJOR on guardrail answers is only partially closed (role posture and CL-011 runtime-role statement still absent even as N/A for a no-DB-change item).
MINOR: CL-011 runtime role posture (NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS) is never stated, not even declared N/A; tenant binding is now covered but guardrail 3 remains unanswered in the delta.
design_pack.observability assigns contract_validation_failures_total{code} to platform, but no artifact in affected_files emits it; the emission point/deferred owner is unstated (guardrail 10).
spec_pack security_threat_model and implementation_plan evidence cite only core/contracts.py although go/pfcore/contracts.go and the parity test are declared in-scope mirrors.
review.impact_review mixes verdicts ("violates" with recommendation "not needed"); verdict/recommendation semantics for impact rows are ambiguous and weaken gate evidence.
NIT: Impact-review evidence cites line numbers (core/bom.py:195,198) that will drift; prefer symbol/contract names for durable evidence.
SUMMARY: Delta meaningfully closes several prior pendings (unknown-field policy, seq invariant, risks list, FR-2 runtime deferral, constant-time test pin, observability owners/thresholds), but three prior majors persist or evolved: config-contract contradiction (now worsened by a dropped spec_pack row and "no new env flag"), incomplete parity-test coverage for non-envelope contracts, and an unresolved language-rule "violates" verdict in the review record.
Top risks before Gate: ship-scope ambiguity on the language rule, a fail-closed security config with no owning design row, and AC parity claimed for contracts with no pinned Go evidence.

MAJOR: review.reconciliation.assumptions B3 says the `seq` writer stays in `core/events.py`, contradicting the binding invariant/decision that seq is assigned by the Go/PostgreSQL event core; this also implies new shipped Python logic under the language rule.

Three Go contract-shape surfaces are now in play (existing `go/contract/contract.go`, `go/pfcore/pfcore.go` contractShapes, new `go/pfcore/contracts.go`); no consolidation or statement of which surface parity tests pin vs. which runtime uses — drift risk defeats AC-1.

`config_contract` mandates WEBHOOK_HMAC_KEY_REF startup validation fail-closed, but this item has no runtime component and, unlike metrics (deferred to BI-PF-1270/1274), no implementing artifact or deferred owner is named.
MINOR: Open question requires parity coverage of cursor ordering, but test_matrix has no named cursor-ordering test.
Row 3 (constant-time HMAC/idempotency) evidence omits `go/pfcore/contracts.go` despite the open question requiring signature-verification parity across Python/Go.
design_pack.security repeats near-identical HMAC/tenant bullets (concatenated revisions), obscuring the actual control set.
NIT: functional_spec.observability and design_pack.observability are verbatim duplicates; ADR-0005 (prior_decisions) and ADR-0011 (assumptions) are cited without cross-reference.
SUMMARY: Delta closes the prior BLOCKER (impact verdict now "aligned") and the config-contract, rollback, CL-011, observability-owner, spec evidence, and webhook-parity-row findings; prior NIT unchanged and not reopened.
Top residual risks: seq-writer contradiction on a P0 invariant, fragmented Go mirror surfaces vs. declared file, and unowned fail-closed startup validation.

MINOR: review.reconciliation.existing_path still labels `go/contract/contract.go` and `pfcore.contractShapes` as the "Go mirror required-field tables", contradicting the new delta decision that `go/pfcore/contracts.go` is canonical and the others legacy/not extended; stale row should be updated in the same delta to avoid implementers extending the wrong surface.

test_matrix row 4 (`test_cursor_ordering_contract`) evidence lists only `core/contracts.py` and `go/pfcore/contracts.go`, omitting `test-framework/tests/pipeline/test_contracts.py` where the test itself lives, breaking the evidence-to-file traceability pattern used by the other rows.
AC "existing test_api_events stays green" is not represented in test_matrix or traceability; add a regression row/evidence so the AC is fail-able in CI, not only implied.

Delta does not explicitly answer the design guardrail checklist items (reversibility/backup, SPOF/startup check, blast-radius/dry-run, tenant isolation, reuse/observability owner) even where they are N/A for a contract-only item; CL-008 requires each item be answered in the design before Gate 1.5 (CL-011/CL-013 are only partially evidenced via security bullets).
NIT: functional_spec.observability and design_pack.observability are no longer verbatim duplicates but remain near-duplicative; consider a single canonical row with the other referencing it.
reconciliation.prior_decisions cites ADR-0005 while assumptions cite ADR-0011 with no cross-reference between the two rows.
SUMMARY: Delta resolves the prior B3 `seq`-writer contradiction, names the canonical Go contract surface, adds the cursor-ordering test row, fixes the HMAC row evidence, and assigns a deferred owner for `WEBHOOK_HMAC_KEY_REF`; prior MAJORs 1-3 and MINORs 4-6 are adequately dispositioned. No blockers: language rule, additive-only invariants, and CI-blocking parity remain intact. Top residual risks are the stale `existing_path` reconciliation row (drift toward legacy Go surfaces) and incomplete guardrail-checklist/AC regression traceability before Gate 1.5.

MAJOR: Unknown-field allowlists are hardcoded independently (Python `ContractSpec` fields vs Go `eventContractFields`) with only static, duplicated fixtures on each side; a field added to one language only passes every added test, so the design failure case "Python/Go shape mismatch → parity test fails CI" (CONTRACT_PARITY_MISMATCH) is not actually enforced for field-set drift.

Binding design parity coverage is incomplete: open-question resolutions require parity tests for cursor ordering (seq-only) and unknown envelope version — neither side has them; Python also lacks the subscription/alert-rule/webhook unknown-field tests that Go adds (`test_contracts_subscription_alert_webhook_parity`).

Go `eventContractFields["subscription"]` (and `alert-rule`) omits `tenant_id`, while the design/guardrails require tenant fields in the subscription contract — a tenant-scoped subscription accepted by Python would be rejected by Go, an untested cross-language shape break on a security-relevant field.

Design obliges this item to define the contract metric names/labels (`contract_validation_failures_total{code}`, `contract_parity_test_failures`, owner platform+CI); the diff defines none, leaving BI-PF-1270/1274 without the promised contract.
MINOR: `WEBHOOK_HMAC_KEY_REF` is not declared in `core/contracts.py`, though spec_pack cites that file as its evidence (startup fail-closed validation is BI-PF-1270's, but the contract name belongs here).

FR-2 acceptance ("signature and event_id idempotency headers are present") is only half-tested: no assertion that `X-PF-Idempotency-Key` equals `event_id`; header constants are checked by tautological equality.
Go mirror defines no `WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_HEADER`/`WEBHOOK_IDEMPOTENCY_HEADER` constants, so the header-name contract exists only in Python — an avoidable parity surface.

`webhook_signature`/`verify_webhook_signature` accept an empty secret and still produce/verify signatures; fail-closed at the primitive would be cheaper than relying solely on BI-PF-1270 startup checks (CL-013 posture).
NIT: Added test names diverge from the design test_matrix names (`test_contracts_unknown_field_parity`, `test_contracts_seq_parity`, `test_contracts_subscription_alert_webhook_parity`), weakening traceability evidence for FR-1/FR-2.
New file `go/pfcore/event_contracts_test.go` is not in the declared `affected_files`.
Go `containsField` is a linear scan over a fixed allowlist; a set/map lookup would be idiomatic and O(1) — negligible at this size.
SUMMARY: Additive, reversible contract work that stays within the approved file scope and language guardrails, and the added tests plausibly satisfy the literal AC (tests pass), but parity is fixture-based rather than cross-checked, so Python/Go field-set drift can ship green.

Top risks: missing mandated parity tests (cursor ordering, unknown version, subscription tenant shape), undefined observability/config contract names assigned to this item, and no test proving the idempotency-header/event_id invariant.

MINOR: New test `test_eventing_tenant_and_idempotency_contract` asserts no idempotency-header behavior (no `X-PF-Idempotency-Key == event_id` check), so the prior FR-2 idempotency gap stays open while the test name falsely claims coverage.

Fail-closed signing now diverges across languages: Python `webhook_signature` raises `ValueError` on empty secret, Go `WebhookSignature` returns `""`; `verify_*` converges to False, but the sign primitive is a new parity surface with no cross-language test.
Python `webhook_signature` gains a new raising path in shipped code; the diff shows no audit of existing callers that may pass an empty/unset secret and now hit a runtime exception.

`CONTRACT_METRICS` is defined only on the Python side; Go has no mirror, so the metric-name contract is another one-sided declaration (only names are pinned, no label/owner structure beyond the embedded `{code}` string).
NIT: `CONTRACT_METRICS` is a mutable module-level dict; a frozen mapping would match the "constants" intent.
New test uses manual `try/except/else raise AssertionError` instead of `pytest.raises`, inconsistent with the rest of the suite.
Metric value embeds the label template in the name string (`contract_validation_failures_total{code}`), which is awkward to consume programmatically by BI-PF-1270/1274.
SUMMARY: Delta correctly closes prior findings on Go `tenant_id` drift, `WEBHOOK_HMAC_KEY_REF`, header constants, metric names, and empty-secret fail-closed on both sides; no AC regression introduced.
Top residual risks: the misleadingly named new test leaves FR-2 idempotency untested, and the Python/Go sign primitives now fail closed via different mechanisms without a parity test.
Overall acceptable for the delta scope; prior PENDING parity/coverage findings (cursor/unknown-version/unknown-field cross-language fixtures) remain open but unchanged.

MAJOR: Delta hunk `go/pfcore/event_contracts_test.go::TestWebhookHeadersAndMetricsParity` is single-language: every assertion is satisfiable by Go alone (Go-only calls + hardcoded `"contract_validation_failures_total"` literal), and no assertion reads Python's `CONTRACT_METRICS`/`webhook_headers`. CI would stay green if the Python side drifted, contradicting the design invariant "contract drift is caught by required-field parity tests, not prose" for exactly the surfaces this test names.
MINOR: Delta introduces `CONTRACT_METRIC_LABELS` in `core/contracts.py` with no Go mirror, leaving a new one-sided declaration (residual of the prior CONTRACT_METRICS finding: names mirrored, label structure not).

`webhook_headers`/`WebhookHeaders` accept empty `event_id` and empty `secret`, emitting empty `X-PF-Idempotency-Key`/`X-PF-Signature` values without rejection, while design declares `event_id required` and config `empty_behavior: fail closed`; only the happy path is tested in the delta.

The delta changes the approved metric contract literal (`contract_validation_failures_total{code}` → name + separate labels) but adds no Python-side assertion pinning `CONTRACT_METRICS`/`CONTRACT_METRIC_LABELS` values, so the Python half of the new metric contract is untested.

Python `webhook_signature` now returns `""` on empty secret (previously `ValueError`); fail-closed holds at `verify_webhook_signature`, but no delta test covers the empty-secret signing output against the Go primitive (sign-side parity only implied).
NIT: `webhook_headers` is defined after the `if __name__ == "__main__": raise SystemExit(_cli())` guard, leaving the module's main block mid-file rather than at the end.
Freeze asymmetry: Python `CONTRACT_METRICS` is a `MappingProxyType` while Go `ContractMetrics` is a mutable package-level `map[string]string`.
SUMMARY: Delta correctly resolves prior dispositions: idempotency-header assertion added, sign-primitive cross-language divergence removed (both return `""`), metric label template split out, Python dict frozen, `pytest.raises`-style cleanup done; no blockers and no language-rule or security regressions.

Top residual risk: the new "parity" test cannot detect Python/Go drift (single-language assertions + hardcoded literals), and the new labels/empty-secret edge paths lack cross-language and fail-closed test coverage.

MAJOR: `test_pfcore_eventing_field_parity` builds/calls only `go/pfcore`; the approved decision requires parity coverage across *both* Go mirrors (go/pfcore and go/contract), so `go/contract/contract.go` drift is undetected by this test.

The parity assertion is a field-name set equality only (`set(desc["result"]["fields"]) == set(field_names())`); nothing checks required-vs-optional flags or type/shape, so the AC phrase "required-field/**shape** parity" is only demonstrated for names.
MINOR: `@pytest.mark.skipif(_go_bin() is None)` means the parity AC can be met vacuously in Go-less environments; CI must record an actual pass (not a skip) as AC evidence.

`test_metric_and_empty_secret_contract` pins `webhook_signature(b"x", "") == ""`, codifying silent empty-secret signing as expected behavior; the same test should assert the verify side rejects an empty secret so fail-closed is proven, not implied.
NIT: The parity test compiles the Go binary inside the test body on every run; a session-scoped build fixture would keep CI deterministic and fast without changing coverage.
SUMMARY: Delta meaningfully adds Python-side parity and metric-pinning evidence, likely resolving the prior single-language-metric finding via constant-pinning on both sides. Top risks: parity covers only one of the two required Go mirrors, and the "shape" half of the AC (required flags/types) is not asserted; ensure CI produces a recorded pass rather than a skip for AC evidence.

MINOR: Go `contractShape` in pfcore.go carries only a flat `fields` slice (unkeyed literal = 2 struct fields), so `describe`'s `required` must be synthesized as `fields`; the new `required` assertion therefore only proves Python marks every eventing field required — optionality is unrepresentable in Go, and a future optional field forces either over-strict Python validation or a weakened parity test.

The added `verify_webhook_signature(b"x", "sha256=00", "") is False` uses an already-invalid signature, so it passes even if verify would accept a correctly computed HMAC under an empty key; assert against `hmac.new(b"", b"x", sha256)`-derived signature to actually prove empty-secret fail-closed (prior MINOR only partially addressed).

[OUT_OF_SCOPE] `TestRequiredFieldParityWithContractHost`'s expected map was edited in lockstep with `pfcore.go`, so this delta's Go test cannot fail by construction; cross-language safety for this change rests entirely on the Python parity test.
NIT: `subscription@1`/`alert-rule@1` required sets were tightened in place under unchanged schema IDs; harmless while unreleased, but treat @1 as frozen once BI-PF-1270 ships consumers to preserve the additive-only invariant.
SUMMARY: Delta is coherent and in-language (Go impl + test-only Python): tenant_id added to subscription/alert-rule required sets in both implementation and pin, plus a cross-language required-set assertion and an empty-secret verify assertion; no blockers found.

Prior findings: empty-secret MINOR only partially resolved (wrong-signature assertion does not prove fail-closed); prior MAJORs (go/contract mirror coverage, shape/type parity) remain PENDING — this delta adds required-set parity but still no type/shape check.
CI must record an actual non-skipped pass of `test_pfcore_eventing_field_parity` and `test_api_events` as AC evidence.

MINOR: Empty-secret fail-closed is now proven only on the Python side; the delta adds no equivalent assertion against the Go verifier mirror, so cross-language security parity for this exact case still rests on the Python test alone.
NIT: `import hashlib` / `import hmac` are placed inside the test body; hoist to module-level imports for consistency with the rest of `test_contracts.py`.
SUMMARY: The delta correctly resolves the prior MINOR by asserting against a correctly computed HMAC under an empty key rather than a pre-broken signature, making the fail-closed check genuinely fail-able.
No blockers, no regressions to AC-1 (parity tests / test_api_events) introduced by this hunk.
Residual risk is symmetry only: mirror the empty-key assertion in the Go parity/security test to close the last cross-language gap.

fix_impact.finding: Unknown-field allowlists are hardcoded independently (Python `ContractSpec` fields vs Go `eventContractFields`) with only static, duplicated fixtures on each side; a field added to one language only passes every added test, so the design failure case "Python/Go shape mismatch → parity test fails CI" (CONTRACT_PARITY_MISMATCH) is not actually enforced for field-set drift.
fix_impact.regression_test: python -m pytest test-framework/tests/pipeline/test_contracts.py -q; go test ./... in go/pfcore and go/contract
fix_impact.rollback: Revert the contract PR; no data migration.

fix_impact.finding: Binding design parity coverage is incomplete: open-question resolutions require parity tests for cursor ordering (seq-only) and unknown envelope version — neither side has them; Python also lacks the subscription/alert-rule/webhook unknown-field tests that Go adds (`test_contracts_subscription_alert_webhook_parity`).
fix_impact.regression_test: python -m pytest test-framework/tests/pipeline/test_contracts.py -q; go test ./... in go/pfcore and go/contract
fix_impact.rollback: Revert the contract PR; no data migration.

fix_impact.finding: Go `eventContractFields["subscription"]` (and `alert-rule`) omits `tenant_id`, while the design/guardrails require tenant fields in the subscription contract — a tenant-scoped subscription accepted by Python would be rejected by Go, an untested cross-language shape break on a security-relevant field.
fix_impact.regression_test: python -m pytest test-framework/tests/pipeline/test_contracts.py -q; go test ./... in go/pfcore and go/contract
fix_impact.rollback: Revert the contract PR; no data migration.

fix_impact.finding: Design obliges this item to define the contract metric names/labels (`contract_validation_failures_total{code}`, `contract_parity_test_failures`, owner platform+CI); the diff defines none, leaving BI-PF-1270/1274 without the promised contract.
